terms.grammar: esse put first, the thing after it
evidence: Hor. S. 1.1.106: est modus in rēbus, sunt certī dēnique fīnēs
Vulg. Jo. 6.9: Est puer ūnus hīc
terms.comment: Brings something new into view, as at the start of a story (est in Carpathiō Neptūnī gurgite vātēs, Verg. G. 4.387). Elsewhere Latin seldom frames a sentence this way: it prefers a verb that says what the thing does or where it is (jacet, stat, situs est) to an English “there was”.

terms.grammar: phrase: est with quod and the subjunctive
terms.comment: Also nihil est quod (see “reason”), and sunt quī, there are those who (see “certain”).

terms.grammar: neuter of ecquis, with a partitive genitive

phrases.latin: Est puer ūnus hīc quī habet quīnque pānēs hordeāceōs et duōs piscēs: sed haec quid sunt inter tantōs?
phrases.english: There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish: but what are they among so many?

phrases.latin: est modus in rēbus, sunt certī dēnique fīnēs
phrases.english: there is a measure in things; there are, in short, fixed bounds

phrases.latin: sunt bona, sunt quaedam mediōcria, sunt mala plūra quae legis hīc: aliter nōn fit, Avīte, liber
phrases.english: there are good things, there are some middling ones, and there are more bad ones that you read here: no other way is a book made, Avitus

phrases.latin: est in Carpathiō Neptūnī gurgite vātēs caeruleus Prōteus
phrases.english: in Neptune’s Carpathian sea there is a seer, sea-blue Proteus

phrases.latin: cui placidus ille: nōn est quod timeās, ait
phrases.english: and to him the lion said calmly: “There’s nothing for you to fear”
